item.title: Patriots opponent preview: The Bears are legit
item.description: Players to watch, stats, injuries, and more for the Patriots’ opponent on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Winners of three straight games, the New England Patriots had little time to enjoy their victory over the New York Jets on Sunday. They quickly turned their attention to their upcoming Week 7 game on Thursday Night Football.

The quick turnaround is not the only challenge this week, though. Even though they are ranked only third in the NFC North at the moment, the Bears look like one of the best teams in football right now: good on offense, good on defense, solid in the return game.

Sounds familiar?

Well, let’s take a closer look.

Bears key stats

The Patriots and Bears are entering their prime time meeting with identical 4-2 records, and similar numbers across the board. What those go to show is that the Bears in Year 2 under head coach Ben Johnson are a legitimate contender — and quite similar to their opponent this week.

Even though quarterback Caleb Williams has played only three games so far this season, Chicago’s offense still ranks in the top half of the league in multiple categories. It is moving the ball well and able to extend drives on third down (45.5%; 6th). Like its Patriots counterpart, however, it also has had its issues with finishing: the Bears are tied for 22nd with a 50.0% red zone rate and tied for sixth-worst in the NFL in total giveaways (11) and turnover rate (16.2%).

Defensively, the unit has performed very well especially against the pass — another similarity with the Patriots, who, like the Bears, have had issues against the run. Turnovers have played a role in Chicago’s strong overall rankings on that side of the. ball, but so has its ability to generate pressure: the team’s 17 sacks and 30.2% pressure rate are both top-5 in the league through six weeks.

Bears 2026 season

As noted above, Caleb Williams has not been able to play the entirety of Chicago’s season. He hurt his hamstring late in Week 2, and subsequently had to sit out the next three games as well. During that span, the Bears did go 2-1 — a testament to their backup quarterbacks and the team’s overall talent (and the fact that the Eagles and Jets are both beatable teams in 2026).

Week 1: 59-37 win at Carolina Panthers (1-0)
Week 2: 9-3 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings (1-1)
Week 3: 27-7 win vs. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1)
Week 4: 23-12 win vs. New York Jets (3-1)
Week 5: 31-7 loss at Green Bay Packers (3-2)
Week 6: 31-23 win at Atlanta Falcons (4-2)

The Bears started their campaign with a shootout win over the Panthers, but just a week later found themselves on the wrong end of a 9-3 loss. Their 56-point swing between those two games was the biggest in since 1973.

Chicago rebounded with those two wins over the Eagles and Jets, followed by a lopsided loss in Green Bay. Their 0-2 record in a competitive division is why the Bears are only third in the NFC North right despite still being sixth in the NFC playoff picture.

On Sunday against the Falcons, Chicago rebounded in style. With Williams back in the lineup, the team jumped to a 31-7 lead before surrendering two late touchdowns. The Bears dominated time of possession and ran 73 plays compared to Atlanta’s 50.

Bears active roster

Roster up-to-date as of Oct. 21, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter

Quarterback (3): Caleb Williams* (18), Tyson Bagent (17), Case Keenum (11)

Running back (3): D’Andre Swift* (4), Kyle Monangai (25), Roschon Johnson (23)

Wide receiver (5): Rome Odunze* (15), Luther Burden III* (10), Kalif Raymond (14 | PR), Zavion Thomas (13 | KR), Jahdae Walker (9)

Tight end (3): Colston Loveland* (84), Cole Kmet* (85), Sam Roush (87)

Offensive tackle (3): Theo Benedet* (79 | LT), Darnell Wright* (58 | RT), Ozzy Trapilo (75)

Interior offensive line (6): Joe Thuney* (62 | LG), Garrett Bradbury* (67 | C), Jonah Jackson* (73 | RG), Luke Newman (65), Logan Jones (54), Jordan McFadden (74)

Interior defensive line (5): Grady Jarrett* (50), Kentavius Street* (93), Neville Gallimore (90), Jordan van den Berg (96), Jayden Loving (91)

Defensive edge (5): Austin Booker* (94), James Lynch* (97), Shemar Turner (95), Daniel Hardy (92), Jamree Kromah (59)

Linebacker (6): Devin Bush Jr.* (12), T.J. Edwards* (53), D’Marco Jackson (48), Noah Sewell (44), Jack Sanborn (57), Keyshaun Elliott (49)

Cornerback (7): Jaylon Johnson* (1), Kyler Gordon* (6), Malik Muhammad II* (24), Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (29), Josh Blackwell (39), Clark Phillips III (20), Nick McCloud (26)

Safety (4): Dillon Thieneman* (31), Cam Lewis* (21), Elijah Hicks (22), Skyler Thomas (38)

Specialists (3): Cairo Santos (8 | K), Tory Taylor (19 | P/H), Scott Daly (46 | LS)

Even tough Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum have both played meaningful snaps this season, the Bears offense is all about Caleb Williams. The first overall selection in the 2024 NFL Draft is the prototypical modern-era quarterback due to his immense arm talent and physical skill combined with the ability to keep plays alive and stress defenses with his legs if need be.

In his three starts this season, Williams completed a league-leading 72.5% of his passes for 712 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also scored on a pair of rushes, contributing to a combined EPA per play of 0.247 — fifth-highest among all qualifying quarterbacks right now. If there are any negatives, it’s Williams taking nine sacks thus far and fumbling the ball twice.

His supporting cast is talented across the board, even with left tackle Braxton Jones out due to injury. It starts at running back, where D’Andre Swift is the main man and a dangerous player as a runner and receiver: he has carried the ball 94 times for 398 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 4.2 yards per carry. Kyle Monangai has also produced at a high level, though, gaining 324 yards and scoring three times on 60 carries for an average of 5.4 yards per run — impressive numbers.

The receiving corps mainly consists of five players, with some alternating as starters. The core guys are Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, whose catches/yards/touchdowns stat lines are solid — 20/312/0 and 19/175/1 — but naturally impacted by Williams’ absence. Atop of the list, meanwhile, are Luther Burden (31/361/1) and Kalif Raymond (26/244/1), who rank first and second on the team in receptions. Also part of the mix is Cole Kmet (7/59/1), whose statistics are mediocre but who plays an important role as a blocker.

The offensive line, as noted above, has been forced to replace its left tackle with backup Theo Benedet. It still has one of the best left guards in the game, ageless wonder and future Pro Football Hall of Famer Joe Thuney, as well as another ex-Patriot, Garrett Bradbury, manning the center position. The right side led by Jonah Jackson and Darnell Wright has been quite solid as well; in fact, it is where the Bears have done their most damage on the ground.

On defense, Chicago will be without starting edges Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat, who are ranked first and second on the team with 14 and 13 quarterback pressures, respectively. As can be seen, the personnel questions are another similarity with the Patriots, even though the Bears have not had to deal with the same volume of injuries this year.

With Odeyingbo and Sweat out, a mix of Austin Booker, James Lynch and Shemar Turner will man the edge. Booker ranks first on the team with four sacks this season, meaning that he is capable of making an impact regardless of who else is on the field with him.

Devin Bush Jr. and T.J. Edwards definitely will be for most of the snaps. Bush Jr. is enjoying a career renaissance as the team’s top linebacker, whereas Edwards has been solid albeit a bit less consistent (as evidenced by his team-leading six missed tackles) as his running mate. D’Marco Jackson has also seen regular action as a rotational option capable of lining up both off the ball and on the edge.

The secondary received some reinforcements last week, with Kyler Gordon returning from the PUP list and immediately making an impact: he tied an NFL record for most sacks in a single game by a cornerback with three, and also forced two fumbles. He is now part of a group also featuring two-time Pro Bowler Jaylon Johnson as the No. 1 cornerback, and fourth-round rookie Malik Muhammad as a surprise starter alongside them.

At safety, first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman has come as advertised and together with veteran Cam Lewis is forming a solid 1-2 duo as the last line of defense.

As far as the kicking game is concerned, Kalif Raymond and Zavion Thomas are the main returners, with the former averaging 12.3 yards on 12 punt runbacks and the latter gaining 24.8 yards per kickoff. For comparison, the Patriots’ featured returners are averaging 9.8 (Marcus Jones) and 24.1 (Kyle Williams) this year. The kicking operation led by Cairo Santos is a bit of a question mark after missing three of 11 field goal attempts this season so far.

Bears reserves

Practice squad (16): QB Miller Moss (16), RB Salvon Ahmed (36), RB Zavier Scott (30), WR Kaden Davis (81), WR Scotty Miller (82), WR J.P. Richardson (83), TE Stephen Carlson (88), TE Qadir Ismail (80), OT Christian Jones (72), OL Caden Barnett (76), LB Buddy Johnson (47), LB Wayne Matthews (35), CB K.C. Eziomume (32), CB Elijah Jones (37), S Keidron Smith (33), LS Beau Gardner (45)

IR (9): RB Brittain Brown (38), TE Nikola Kalinic (86), TE Hayden Large (43), LT Braxton Jones (70), ED Dayo Odeyingbo (55), LB Tony Fields II (43), LB Nephi Sewell (46), S Coby Bryant (2), S Anthony Johnson Jr. (27 | PS IR)

Suspended (1): ED Montez Sweat (98)

The biggest names on the Bears’ reserve lists are the aforementioned Dayo Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat. Odeyingbo was recently placed on IR with a quad injury, while Sweat is currently suspended for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing substance policy and not eligible to return until after this week’s game. Also on injured reserve are two other starters: left tackle Braxton Jones and safety Coby Bryant, neither of whom will be able to play this week.

As mentioned earlier, the Bears have not been hit quite as hard as the Patriots, but they too have had to adapt after suffering some key losses — including, possibly, Kyle Monangai and T.J. Edwards this week, who were non-participants during practice on Tuesday.

Bears coaching staff

Head coach: Ben Johnson

Coordinators: Press Taylor (OC), Dennis Allen (DC), Richard Hightower (ST)

The Bears hired Ben Johnson as their head coach last year. If not for fellow new arrival Mike Vrabel, he could have earned Coach of the Year honors for turning a 5-12 record the previous season into 11-6 and a playoff berth. Johnson did see some changes from 2025 to 2026, however, with offensive coordinator Declan Doyle leaving for the Ravens; Press Taylor was promoted from pass game coordinator to OC in his place. Of course, Johnson remains actively involved on that side of the ball.

Johnson’s staff also includes some familiar names. Offensive analyst Will Lawing served as Patriots tight ends coach in 2022, while quality control coach and former wide receiver Isaiah Ford had a one-month stint with the team in 2020.

item.title: Potential trade targets for the Cincinnati Bengals
item.description: The Bengals should reunite Al Golden with corner Cam Hart from the Chargers
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off of their bye week, sitting in last place in the AFC North at 3-2. With everyone else in the division sitting at 4-2, they are right in the mix to still win the division.

Meanwhile, there are several teams around the league sitting with just 1 win on the season, along with the Chargers, who are surprisingly 0-6 to start the year. Could the Bengals swing a trade to continue making a push back to the playoffs this year?

Most years, I would say absolutely not. After adding Dexter Lawrence via trade for the 10th overall selection, it cannot be completely ruled out. Let’s take a look around the league at some potential players that could be on the trade block for teams that have started out poorly this year.

Washington Commanders (1-4-1 record)

The Commanders invested heavily in free agency this season, and it has not worked out on the field. One of those additions was tight end Chig Okonkwo. With Tanner Hudson recently going on IR the Bengals could use another receiving threat at the tight end position. Okonkwo is coming off his best game of the season on Monday Night Football. He went for 6 receptions for 69 yards in the Week 6 loss.

Unfortunately, Okonkwo is under contract for two more seasons after this one. I can’t see the Bengals actually bringing in a high-dollar tight end to the roster with Jack Endries just sitting on the 53-man roster already.

Outside of Okonkwo I don’t see anybody else on their roster that makes sense from a football standpoint who could become available from Washington.

Tennessee Titans (1-5 record)

Tennessee was able to finally get in the win column this week. They are still a team that looks more in the running for the top overall draft pick than they do a shot at making a run toward the playoffs this year.

Linebacker Cedric Gray has been demoted from a full-time starter to a rotational role in the defense after the addition of rookie Anthony Hill Jr. from Texas this season. Gray finished the 2025 season fourth overall in total tackles with 164. He had a 92.7 run defense grade last season.

The Bengals’ young linebackers are improving, but it would be nice to add another player in the mix to take snaps from Oren Burks. It would also be better injury insurance over Burks for the current starters. Buying low on a player still on his rookie contract that has played well in the past makes a lot of sense to me.

Amani Hooker at strong safety is another player that makes sense from a purely football standpoint. Jordan Battle has struggled, and Kyle Dugger has been injured. Hooker has over 5,000 career snaps, has an 88.5 run defense grade this season, and has recorded 2 interceptions.

However, Hooker just recently signed a 3-year contract extension in Tennessee. That could make it unlikely the Bengals have any interest there.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5 record)

Tampa Bay blew a 16-3 lead in the second half against the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. With just one win on the season, we might see them decide to unload a few contracts around the trade deadline. The player everyone would love to add to this roster is Bucky Irving. Irving is one of the most elusive running backs in the league. Still on his rookie deal through next season, I can’t see the Buccaneers actually trading him.

There is another running back they might part with, and that is Kenny Gainwell. Gainwell had some quality games against the Bengals last season when he was playing for Pittsburgh. He has just 61 rushing yards and 61 receiving yards so far this season. Last year with Pittsburgh he ran for 537 yards, while adding an additional 486 receiving.

Gainwell is under contract again for next year with a salary of $7 million. He could be cut with a dead cap hit of $3 million before that season. I don’t know how much interest the Bengals would actually have in Gainwell, but he does seem like a player that is likely to be on the trading block.

Miami Dolphins (0-5 record)

Miami is in a complete rebuild this season. They have added a lot of young talent via the 2026 NFL Draft, and will be looking to do the same again this year. They are likely to sell off some players for draft capital ahead of the trade deadline.

The problem here is that I don’t think anyone they might be willing to part with makes sense for Cincinnati. I could see them letting go of a veteran like Josh Uche or Zach Sieler on the defensive line. For once, that is not a position that the Bengals are in desperate need of. If anything, we have so many guys at that position that it is hard for some of the young guys to see enough snaps this year. Jordyn Brooks would have been a prime target to go after, but the Miami Dolphins decided to give him another contract extension this year. They are planning to have him and rookie Jacob Rodriguez as building blocks for their defense going forward.

Los Angeles Chargers (0-6 record)

People are going to toss out names like running back Omarion Hampton, safety Derwin James, and pass rusher Khalil Mack. I don’t see any of those being realistic options for Cincinnati to acquire. Hampton is in his second season, and the Chargers are unlikely to give up on him just yet. James has a massive contract and has been constantly injured. Mack isn’t a position Cincinnati really needs help at, along with a hefty contract of his own this year.

The one player that I would go after is cornerback Cam Hart. Hart played for Al Golden at Notre Dame. He has great size at 6’2” and 207 pounds. He is having a career year with a 73.8 coverage grade. He is still just 25 years old, and has also recorded 2 interceptions this year. With the Chargers at 0-6 I am making that phone call and trying to acquire Hart.

If you added Hart, it would allow Dax Hill to stay in the slot the rest of the year. Hart would start on the outside opposite of DJ Turner. That trio could be one of the best in the league. Shoring up the secondary with the defensive line Cincinnati has would be beneficial for a team looking to make a long playoff run.

item.title: Kevin Byard sharing "as much as I can" with Patriots ahead of return to Chicago
item.description: Patriots safety Kevin Byard isn't from Chicago, but Thursday night's game will still be a homecoming of sorts for the veteran.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots safety Kevin Byard isn't from Chicago, but Thursday night's game will still be a homecoming of sorts for the veteran.

Byard played for the Bears for the last two seasons and was named a first-team All-Pro after helping them win the NFC North last season. Byard moved on as a free agent this offseason, but said he has no bad feelings about his departure and is excited to be back in "an electric environment" at Soldier Field.

The lack of bad feelings doesn't mean he'll do anything he can to give the Patriots a leg up in their bid for a fourth straight win.

“I’m giving the coaches and the players as much as I can, you know what I mean?” Byard said, via Kyle Hightower of the Associated Press. “Obviously, I am not there anymore, and I don’t have all my notes and stuff like that. But as far as personnel, anything I can kind of remember.”

Byard led the league with seven interceptions last season, but he has yet to pick a ball off this year. Getting one off of former teammate Caleb Williams might prove to be a bigger help to New England's cause than any intel Byard might offer off the field.

The Dallas Cowboys have struggled with health in their secondary all season. On Tuesday, they decided Caelen Carson was no longer in the mix. While it opened a roster spot for Juanyeh Thomas, it could also mean Cobie Durant returns to the field soon.

Cowboys sign S Juanyeh Thomas to active roster, waive CB Caelen Carson – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com

Juanyeh Thomas is officially back on the 53-man roster after a few weeks on the practice squad.

Over the course of his three previous seasons with Dallas, Thomas played in 36 games, including starting three in 2025, and posted 62 tackles, five pass breakups and a forced fumble. Most of his work over that time has come on special teams, including 65 snaps there through three games played in 2026.

In 2024, the Cowboys drafted Carson in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Wake Forest. Over the course of the last three seasons, Carson played in 17 games and started eight for Dallas. Carson tallied 45 career tackles, a tackle for loss and six pass breakups in that time span.

Cowboys have gone away from these key things that once sparked optimism in Dallas’ offense – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News

It’s unsettling how the Cowboys abandoned the run game versus the Green Bay Packers

Sunday’s game was never really out of hand from a scoring perspective, however. Still, that didn’t keep the Cowboys from doing something they’ve done a lot this season: abandon the running game. The Cowboys finished with 54 passes compared to 15 running attempts. They had only one rushing attempt in the fourth quarter. 

Last year, the Cowboys were 16th in rushing attempts. This year, they’re 31st.

Offense in disarray

item.title: Lions scouting report: Packers riding an upward trend
item.description: Breaking down the Green Bay Packers strengths, weaknesses, and ongoing season production.
item.content:encoded:
After a much-needed bye week, the Detroit Lions are back on the field. They kick off their 2026 campaign to reclaim their NFC North crown against the Green Bay Packers in Ford Field in Week 7. After back-to-back road games and a bye week, Lions fans should be going crazy for them on Sunday afternoon.

The Green Bay Packers have had a wild up-and-down season so far in 2026. Injuries and off-the-field concerns dropped the team to 1-2 after Week 3. Since then, the team is on a three-game winning streak and heads to Detroit with star running back Josh Jacobs back on the field to give the offense a much-needed boost. While this is Detroit’s first divisional game, the Packers are 1-1 in divisional play this season.

Let’s take a deep look at the Packers’ season so far ahead of Week 7.

Green Bay Packers

2026 season thus far (4-2)

Week 1: Lost to Minnesota Vikings, 39-22
Week 2: Defeated New York Jets, 20-17 (OT)
Week 3: Lost to Atlanta Falcons, 35-14
Week 4: Defeated Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 17-14
Week 5: Defeated Chicago Bears, 31-7
Week 6: Defeated Dallas Cowboys, 23-13

Offensive stats:

The offense has had a more chaotic ride than the defense. At quarterback, Jordan Love has been doing well, throwing for 1,684 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions. He’s had to carry the offense while the running game has struggled. Love has the third-most passing yards in the NFL, but the passing game hasn’t been all flowers and roses, as it ranks in the middle of the pack in DVOA and PFF.

With Jacobs returning, expect that part of the offense to take a step forward. MarShawn Lloyd leads the team with 122 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 2.5 yards per carry. The trade for Kaleb Johnson hasn’t worked out as well as fans hoped, with Johnson getting only 104 yards on 3.7 yards per carry. The running game is the offense’s biggest weakness, ranking in the bottom four in multiple categories, from rushing yards to DVOA to PFF grades.

When Love has time to throw, he most often finds wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson leads the team in yards (538) and touchdowns (6), while Golden leads in catches with 30. The duo has already combined for over 1,000 yards this season, and they could be the passing game’s future one-two punch if wide receiver Jayden Reed can’t return from his neck injury. Newly paid tight end Tucker Kraft has had a slow start, catching 25 passes for 249 yards and a touchdown. Green Bay’s biggest flaw right now is drops, as they lead the NFL with 20, according to Pro Football Reference.

One major reason for the running game’s struggles is the offensive line. Injuries have plagued the position group, and the team has made multiple moves, including signing former Detroit Lion Kevin Zeitler to provide immediate help, although he has yet to play. According to PFF, they have the second-worst run-blocking grade (47.8), but it gets worse. They also have the worst pass-blocking grade from PFF (46.8), which explains why, despite Love’s high mark in passing yards, the passing grades and DVOA aren’t high, but they’re enough to carry the offense and make them an average team in EPA.

Defensive stats:

The Packers defense has been on the calmer side this year, but not in the front seven. Two defensive tackles and a linebacker are on IR, while their star pass rusher and another defensive tackle are still on PUP. EDGE Lukas Van Ness leads the line with 3.5 sacks, while defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt has 2.0 sacks and a forced fumble as the defense tries to hold down the fort until EDGE Micah Parsons returns.

The linebacker room lost its best player, Edgerrin Cooper, for the year with a torn Achilles, but Zaire Franklin and Ty’Ron Hopper are doing their best to keep the defense tough. Franklin has 41 tackles, a forced fumble, and a pass deflection, while Hopper has 12 tackles, two pass deflections, and an interception.

Green Bay’s secondary has been the strength of the defense, mostly because of the lack of injuries at the position. Safety Xavier McKinney is back to his old tricks, tied for the league lead with three interceptions, and with Evan Williams next to him with two, this safety duo looks like one of the best in the NFL. With a stout secondary, they rank highly in passing defense in DVOA and passing yards allowed, and PFF rates them the NFL’s top coverage unit.

While the passing defense has been stellar, this team is struggling to stop the run, which makes sense with how many bodies are out in that front seven, especially on the interior. With the Packers allowing over 110 rushing yards a game, Detroit may try to use the running game to open up the passing game.

Injury notes

Key players ruled out: RT Zach Bako-Bewele (IR), LB Edgerrin Cooper (IR), WR Jayden Reed (IR), DT Javon Hargrave (IR), DT Jonathan Ford (IR), WR Skyy Moore (IR)
Key players to monitor: TE Luke Musgrave (PUP), EDGE Micah Parsons (PUP), DT Jordon Riley (PUP), G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), T Anthony Belton (knee), C/G Jager Burton (back), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring)

We thought the Carolina Panthers were banged up. Oh man, the Packers blew them out of the water. Their offensive line took a big blow when they lost their top player, right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, to a patellar tendon tear that ended his season.

Several of these injuries are season-ending, but the Packers are dealing with even more issues. Their superstar Parsons is still on PUP, and he won’t be returning to practice this week, but he’ll be on the field soon enough. Another player still on PUP is tight end Luke Musgrave, as the Packers could use all the help they can get on offense. Last week, the Packers added more players to their IR list: defensive tackles Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford, and wide receiver Skyy Moore.

Additionally, the offensive line has four linemen (two starters) dealing with issues: left guard Aaron Banks is battling knee and toe issues, and the replacement for Bako-Bewele, Anthony Belton, is dealing with a knee injury. Banks missed Week 6, so his Week 7 status is up in the air. Their depth at guard and center has been rough, too: backup interior lineman Jager Burton missed Week 6 with a back injury, and Jacob Monk is dealing with a quad injury. Cornerback took a little bit of a hit, down Benjamin St-Juste, but it’s nowhere near as depleted as the trenches.

Biggest strength: Secondary

With injuries depleting the front seven, the secondary is taking on the burden of carrying the defense. They’ve allowed the third-fewest yards per passing attempt. Green Bay leads the NFL in interceptions with nine. When you not only limit what offenses can do through the air but also take away the football, you start changing how offenses attack you.

The Packers have allowed the third-lowest passer rating (73.9) and only nine passing plays over 20+ yards, tied for second-fewest in the league. We’ve seen what great safety play is like in Detroit when safeties Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch are on the field together, and the Packers are doing the same with McKinney and Williams. The cornerback room isn’t too impressive, but they’ve done their job well, so with the overtop help being as dominant as it has been, the cornerbacks have more opportunities to make plays and do their part.

Biggest weakness: Running back

Despite Jacobs returning this week for Green Bay, this position has been a huge problem for them this year. It’s uncertain how ready Jacobs will be and how much he’ll play, but with the offensive line struggling to stay healthy, even he could still struggle on Sunday afternoon.

The team needed five weeks, over a month of football, for one of their running backs to get over 100 total rushing yards in a season. When teams know you can’t run the football and have to rely on the passing game to move the chains, it’s easier to defend. Green Bay has attempted 107 runs with their running backs while throwing the ball 226 times.

You can’t even say it’s because they’ve been behind in all their games; they led Minnesota 22-10 in Week 1 and still allowed 29 straight points. Then, in Week 4 against Tampa Bay, they led by 10 in the third quarter and still won by only 3. Green Bay can’t rely on Love to do all the heavy lifting when he’s constantly facing pressure, getting sacked 13 times this season

Key matchup: Lions secondary vs. Packers passing attack

The Packers offense likes to take multiple deep shots and hope for a holding call or defensive pass interference.

“The quarterback gives them a nice pretty ball, man, lays it out there,” coach Dan Campbell said this week. “And really about 50 percent of these are either DPI or catches, which is talk about explosive.”

With the Lions’ secondary playing so poorly, Green Bay has a great opportunity to strike multiple times downfield and get big chunk plays on penalties.

Detroit’s secondary improved when rookie safety Keith Abney II took over a primary role at safety; he even got his first career interception. With him and Branch returning, the deep shots might be tougher than expected. Green Bay will still attack that way, knowing Branch is fresh off his injury and Abney only has one game of experience at the position.

If Detroit can limit the damage from the Packers’ passing attack, Green Bay’s offense could crumble. On the other side, if Green Bay can strike down the field through the air, this game could become another shootout for Detroit, where whoever has the ball last wins.

Vegas line for Sunday: Lions favored by 3

item.title: NFL Secret Superstars: 3 under-the-radar NFC standouts from Week 6
item.description: McCarthy’s 243-yard relief outing, Hubbard’s 120 yards against the Eagles, and Williams’ interception of Dak Prescott headline the NFC’s under-the-radar standouts
item.content:encoded:
Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it’s the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they’re needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they’re playing in a smaller market, and the media isn’t appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they’re hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it’s always possible that a wayward coach hasn’t quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our NFC Secret Superstars for Week 6 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven’t yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

J.J. McCarthy, Relief QB, New York Giants

When the Minnesota Vikings traded former 10th-overall pick J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on September 28 for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick, there could be no more obvious way of stating that McCarthy’s NFL career had hit rock bottom. The Michigan star whom the Vikings traded up to take in the 2024 draft now couldn’t be out of the building quickly enough, and the Giants had their own quarterback issues with Jaxson Dart’s season-ending knee injury.

The Giants already had Jameis Winston, and if you’re going to ride that ride, you know the risks involved. Jameis will show you the good and bad sides of the Quarterback Rogue Gene, and when Jameis threw an interception with 12:28 left in Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints, head coach John Harbaugh apparently had enough for the moment. McCarthy was in.

Of course, McCarthy’s day didn’t start very well. With 10:27 left in the game, McCarthy threw his own pick.

So, nobody could be blamed for thinking that McCarthy was just going to disappoint again.

Except that from there, he did anything but disappoint. Overall, McCarthy completed 11 of 23 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown, that interception, and four explosive plays that very few people could have expected.

The Giants had blown a 10-0 second-quarter lead to the Saints, who then scored 34 unanswered points, but with 12 seconds left in the game, McCarthy was actually in position to tie things up at 34-34 had his pass to tight end Isaiah Likely been completed.

McCarthy’s outing was far from perfect — start with the fact that on that final play, he missed a wide-open Malik Nabers in the end zone — but offensive coordinator Matt Nagy set McCarthy up to do the two things he does well — air the ball out downfield, and run around when things get complicated. McCarthy was also the Giants’ leading rusher on the day with 26 yards on two carries.

So, it wasn’t one of those overnight turnarounds, but the fact that McCarthy was able to come in cold and do what he did was singularly impressive. Per Next Gen Stats, he wound up tied for the sixth-most fourth quarter passing yards in this century, and his 14.9 air yards per attempt and 17.2 air yards per completion were the most by a quarterback with at least 20 dropbacks in a game this season. McCarthy led the NFL last year with 9.3 air yards per attempt and a 42.4% downfield throw rate, so little surprise there.

“It’s not even up for discussion or conversation right now,” Harbaugh said after the game, when asked whether Winston or McCarthy would take the helm from here on out. “We’ve got to go back and go to work. I have no problem with Jameis whatsoever. I love the way he competes, I love the way he fights, all those kind of things. He was up and down today for sure, but those things will all be decided not 10 minutes after a game.”

As for McCarthy, Harbaugh said that he “did a heck of a job given the circumstances. It’s different than normal football, but [he] made some plays and got us back, gives us a chance to win the game, and we’re throwing the ball in the end zone at the end, so that was good. You’ve got to compliment him on that.”

What it means for McCarthy’s NFL future is unknown, but that was a bright spot in what’s been a disappointing run so far.

Chuba Hubbard, RB, Carolina Panthers

(Note: Hubbard was the winner of this week’s NFC Secret Superstars poll, where you can vote for the third Secret Superstar for both the AFC and NFC every week).

It speaks to the Carolina Panthers’ current construction that they were able to beat the Philadelphia Eagles 25-14 on Sunday with Bryce Young completing just 20 of 39 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions, and a passer rating of 92.8, and an EPA per pass of +0.06. Not bad at all, but given Young’s overall development this season (he’s generally the engine of the offense now), head coach Dave Canales and offensive coordinator Brad Idzik were going to have to find other avenues to get things done.

And it isn’t as if the Eagles’ defense presents a natural pathway to inside runs — not when you can put Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and the underrated Moro Ojomo in the middle of your four- and five-man fronts. Coming into Sunday’s game, per Sports Info Solutions, the Eagles had allowed just 187 rushing yards and 3.3 yards per carry on 57 opponent runs listed as to the middle, or to the right and left inside. So, if the Panthers were going to get running back Chuba Hubbard on the good foot, they would need to bounce things outside. The Eagles had allowed 403 yards and 4.4 yards per carry through Week 5 on 91 opponent runs to off-tackle or outside.

Which is exactly what the Panthers did. Through the first four weeks of the season (the Panthers had a Week 5 bye), Hubbard had run inside on 26% of his carries. Against the Eagles, Hubbard hit the A-gaps on just five of his 28 carries. Overall, that allowed him to gain 120 yards with a rushing touchdown on those 28 carries.

Bouncing it outside as much as Hubbard did was a literal game-changer.

“We started off the game with a really nice run,” Canales said postgame of the overall plan, and Hubbard’s 11-yard run on the Panthers’ first offensive play of the game. “I was like, ‘Here we go.’ First half is gone, and I didn’t really come up with much after that. But the guys coming together, troubleshooting some different fronts, thought [Eagles defensive coordinator Vic] Fangio did an amazing job of just giving us different looks and making it challenging in the run game, but we were able to stick with it. We were able to find some success, and Chuba ended up with, I think, 120 [yards] or something like that by the end of it. And he’s running the ball really well right now. That should complement the rest of the offense.” 

Hubbard is running the ball really well now. The 2021 fourth-round pick out of Oklahoma State has 426 yards and four touchdowns on 89 carries through five games, and he proved in this game (as he has before) that when you need a bell cow back to lean on, he has the goods to make it a positive reality.

Evan Williams, Safety, Green Bay Packers

When the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys kicked off Sunday Night Football, the one thing you could expect was a lot of points, right? The Packers have been riddling their opponents of late with a killer deep passing game, and we all know that the Cowboys are unable to handle that (or any other) offensive concept. The less predictable aspect to the game was how Jonathan Gannon’s Packers defense would handle a Cowboys offense that has been the franchise’s balm through years of abysmal defensive coaching and execution.

As it turned out, Gannon and his crew put on a master class in how to throttle a great passing game. Against Dak Prescott, one of the smartest pre- and post-snap quarterbacks in the NFL, the Packers gave him all sorts of looks he didn’t expect. In Dallas’ 23-13 loss, Prescott completed 34 of 54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 65.2. Had referee Craig Wrolstad and his crew not called a seriesof truly mystifying roughing the passer penaltieson various Packers defenders, Prescott’s game could have been much worse.

One of the key men in the Packers’ dismantling of Dallas’ usually high-flying offense was safety Evan Williams. The 2024 fourth-round pick from Oregon has really found a place in Gannon’s defense. Against the Cowboys, he had seven solo tackles, two quarterback hits, and he allowed one catch on one target for seven yards. Williams wasn’t the target on the interception he got with 14:23 left in the first half, because Williams started at the line of scrimmage, and hauled it all the way back to the deep third in time to jump Prescott’s skinny post throw to CeeDee Lamb that might have been a touchdown otherwise.

Overall, Williams never seemed to finish the play where he started it, and this is one reason Prescott hung in the pocket so often, trying to find openings, when there were no openings to be had.

“First of all, great call by J.G. [Gannon] — kind of put me in a great position to go get that one,” Williams said of the interception. “I saw CeeDee at 3 [the inside slot]; he’s normally a hot-route type of guy that Dak is looking for, especially in that high red [zone]. So, [I] got out, and really, instincts kind of took over. After the ball was snapped, I kind of floated to a good position, where I put myself between the man and the ball, and the ball showed up.”

Amazing what preparation, and the right guy in the right place, will do for a defense.

item.title: NFL Secret Superstars: 3 under-the-radar AFC standouts from Week 6
item.description: Noel’s 107-yard day in London, Tucker’s two touchdowns against Buffalo, and Dean’s record-setting revenge game headline the AFC’s under-the-radar standouts.
item.content:encoded:
Superstars may lead the discussion when it comes to success in the NFL, but more often than not, it’s the guys you barely know who will make the plays needed when they’re needed. Such players can be underrated for all kinds of reasons. Perhaps they’re playing in a smaller market, and the media isn’t appropriately trumpeting their exploits. Maybe they’re hidden in a depth chart behind bigger names who may not be doing as much. Or, it’s always possible that a wayward coach hasn’t quite figured out that one guy needs elevation to bring better results to the team.

Whatever the reason, we at SB Nation always like to bring the underrated names to you with the offseason Hidden Gems and in-season Secret Superstars series. You can also catch up on the AFC and NFC Secret Superstars for the 2026 season right here.

Here are our AFC Secret Superstars for Week 6 of the 2026 regular season. And if you haven’t yet, download the new SB Nation app, so you can better read our stuff and join the conversation wherever you are!

(All advanced metrics courtesy of Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Focus, Sports Info Solutions, and Sumer Sports unless otherwise indicated).

Jaylin Noel, WR, Houston Texans

“Jaylin has come along. I think with any receivers, any guys who touch the football, when you touch it enough and you make some big plays… that’s what Jaylin did in college a lot at Iowa State. You saw him making a lot of big plays, and over the past couple of weeks, we’ve been able to get him in those spots and opportunities to make big plays. He’s come down with the football, made those plays, and when you do that, it builds the confidence. What I’ve seen from Jaylin Noel, I’ve seen the confidence boost, and I see him continue to thrive and make the plays we expected him to make.”

Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans had that to say about Jaylin Noel, his second-year, third-round pick from Iowa State, last Friday when asked how Noel was coming along in Nick Caley’s offense. Noel was coming off a three-catch, 85-yard game against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, and a five-catch, 41-yard, one-touchdown game against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5.

Still, and especially given the recent trade for ex-Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., who expected Noel to be the receiver most worthy of praise after the Texans’ 34-31 win at Wembley Stadium against a very game Jacksonville Jaguars defense? Noel caught four passes on four targets for 107 yards and a touchdown, and he was an explosive play machine all over the field. Not Harrison, who caught three passes on four targets for 34 yards, and not No. 1 receiver Nico Collins, who caught three passes on five targets for 74 yards. It was Noel, the ideal No. 2 receiver in any offense because of his formation versatility, who won the day.

Postgame, Ryans was even more convicted that Noel has a lot to contribute.

“Jaylin Noel, he’s continued to make big play after big play every week,” Ryans said. “The more opportunities he’s gotten, the more plays he’s made for our team. He had a career day today, over 100 yards, most yards in his career. He just keeps making explosive plays. He’s a true weapon for us. Happy we have him.“

The Texans have won two straight games after an 0-4 start, and if this particular receiver trio can put things together at a new level, maybe the rebound can continue.

Tre Tucker, WR, Las Vegas Raiders

(Note: Tucker was the winner of this week’s AFC Secret Superstars poll in the NFL Feed, where you can vote for the third Secret Superstar for both the AFC and NFC every week).

Something very unusual happened in the Las Vegas Raiders’ 33-30 Sunday loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Tight end Brock Bowers, who had set the NFL ablaze in the first five weeks of the season, caught just four passes on nine targets for 70 yards. These were all season lows for Bowers, in part because the Bills were bracketing him, and cornerback Christian Benford was mugging Bowers from the start of his routes as much as possible. This allowed others to step up in Klint Kubiak’s passing game. Fellow tight end Michael Mayer had seven catches on nine targets for 95 yards, but the Raiders’ secret weapon here was receiver Tre Tucker, who caught five passes on seven targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns.

It wasn’t enough to slide by the Bills and Josh Allen’s latest Superman performance, but it was a definitive performance for the 2023 third-round pick from Cincinnati, who was miscast in the eyes of some as purely a slot receiver at 5’9” and about 185 pounds.

Turns out, Tucker can do a lot more than that. He showed it in the 2025 season in the Raiders’ disaster of an offense when he had 57 catches on 90 targets for 696 yards and five touchdowns.

And he’s showing it even more in Kubiak’s offense.

“I mean, it was a great catch by him on the first one,” Kirk Cousins said postgame when asked about his connection with Tucker. “Great design by our coaches to get him in that position where he’s open like that. The second one, he just can roll. I played with DeSean Jackson, I played with Aldrick Robinson, so I’ve played with 4.2 guys; he can roll. And I came off the field, I said, ‘I think he’s faster than I realize he is.’ And there’s times where I just need to launch, and he’ll go get it. So, he showed me that again today, and big-time the way he finished it, to go for it and hold on.

“It just starts to build trust and respect when a guy goes and makes a play like that.”

Tucker is feeling the difference in his own play this season.

“I feel like every year, I was thrust into something,” he said. “But that sudden change — I think this year, my mindset was just different coming into the season. I’m older. I’m a year older. I’ve been working all offseason, and just having a different mindset every time I walk out on the field. That just comes with all the preparation throughout the year, and the people on the field that I get to play with, and obviously the trust that staff has in me.”

Well, the trust is well-earned. Especially when defenses decide to bracket others in the Raiders’ offense. Tre Tucker is here to make you pay for that.

Jamel Dean, CB, Pittsburgh Steelers

For a very long time, Jamel Dean was a great (if perpetually underrated) cornerback for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The 2019 third-round pick out of Auburn was the same force multiplier he had generally been before in the 2025 season, when he allowed 25 catches on 54 targets for 311 yards, 105 yards after the catch, one touchdown, three interceptions, five pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 47.7 — the NFL’s lowest among all cornerbacks who played at least 50% of their teams’ defensive snaps.

Apparently, that wasn’t enough for the Bucs, who decided to let Dean test the free-agent market. The Steelers swept in with a three year, $36.750 million contract including $12 million guaranteed. Quite a bargain for such a player, through Dean’s age (30) and injury history (he played 631 of a possible 1,001 defensive snaps last season) presented understandable caps to his overall value.

Still, the Steelers needed veteran leadership and on-field acumen at the cornerback position, and with Dean, they got both. Dean missed some of Week 4 and all of Week 5 with an ankle injury, but one can imagine that he was fairly excited for last Sunday’s game, which pitted the Steelers against the Bucs.

In his first game against his former team, Dean was tested — a LOT. The Bucs pegged him as a target on 11 of quarterback Jalon Daniels’ 43 passing attempts, and Dean responded by allowing four catches for 48 yards, five yards after the catch, no touchdowns, one interception, six pass breakups, and an opponent passer rating of 12.7. Those six pass deflections marked the most in a game in recorded Steelers history.

Over and over, Daniels tried to test the veteran, and over and over, Dean said, “No soup for you!” Dean was mostly on Emeka Egbuka, but whoever he covered, the results were generally going to be less than optimal for the Buccaneers…

…who should have known better.

To his credit, after the Steelers’ 26-19 win, Dean was all class. He spoke glowingly about Tampa Bay head coach Todd Bowles, who had been Dean’s defensive coordinator from 2019-2021, and his head coach thereafter.

“It was a bittersweet moment,” Dean said of his interception, via FOX Sports’ Greg Auman. “For the first time, I could be on the opposite side to see what that experience is like. At the same time, I was like, ‘I guess I’ve got to go against the guy that taught me the game of football.’

“I don’t want his teachings to go to waste. Hopefully, he’s proud of me, knowing that everything he taught me has translated to another organization.”

One would imagine that Bowles is proud of his former student… with a bit of rueful regret mixed in. Dean may not be an every-down player at this point in his career, but the Steelers could do a lot worse with a cornerback that needs to be on a pitch count. And when he’s 100%, watch the heck out.

item.title: Corey Kiner’s clock-killing carries are what’s great about football
item.description: The Patriots running back stepped up against the Jets on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Football really is the ultimate team sport. There’s something so poetic about how often the fortunes of the largest figures in the sport are shaped by players no one knows before they are suddenly thrust into the limelight. Just ask Malcolm Butler. Nothing reminded me of this truth more than watching the end of last Sunday’s game during a picture-perfect autumn afternoon at Gillette Stadium.

The Patriots had the ball up by one score midway through the fourth quarter against the Jets in an important AFC East contest. New England’s offense is led by a quarterback who narrowly missed winning the MVP a season ago. His top target is a three-time All-Pro with a Super Bowl title to his name. And yet, with the game on the line, Josh McDaniels turned to a cast of cast-offs to seal the win.

As the clock ticked under six minutes to go in the ballgame, McDaniels needed to make that clock keep ticking faster and faster. To make that happen, he turned to his run-game personnel package. That group included a trio of players no one wanted: wide receiver Efton Chism, tight end Cameron Latu, and running back Corey Kiner.

The Foxboro Faithful are familiar with Chism after his heroics in Buffalo a few weeks ago. No one wanted him in the 2025 NFL Draft, but that didn’t stop him from carving out a spot on the roster and earning playing time. When Mack Hollins went down with an injury, Chism was there to help fill in for his run-blocking presence despite being roughly half the size.

Latu and Kiner are less familiar to the fans. With multiple tight ends banged up coming out of camp, the Patriots claimed Latu off waivers when he didn’t make the cut in Philadelphia. He made his presence felt earlier in this game on special team with a thundering hit on a kickoff return, and he’s be out there to help the Patriots put the game away.

After the team’s camp competition for a third running back left people wanting. New England swung a future seventh-round pick to Arizona for the running back buried on the depth chart behind the guy they took third overall this spring and the veteran free agent they signed shortly before that. Like Chism, Kiner also went undrafted in 2025.

Little did they know, this group would decide the outcome.

McDaniels called Kiner’s number eight times in a row. Kiner answered by picking up three first downs and 42 yards, taking almost four minutes off the clock as it ticked down to the two-minute warning. The longest run of the drive, one that went for 12 yards, was aided by a Latu kick-out block. The second longest, an eight-yarder, got some help from Efton Chism blocking out Minkah Fitzpatrick.

Of course, the running game can’t do what it needs to do without the offensive line. Down three starters, the Pats were forced to turn over the interior of the line to two more players most fans had never heard of.

When the Patriots took the field for that game-sealing drive, it was Walter Rouse at left guard and Matt Pryor at right guard. Rouse ended up in New England one day after Kiner. He was moved from Minnesota for a day-three pick swap to help give the Patriots some depth. Meanwhile, Pryor was with the Cardinals on their practice squad until being signed by the Patriots at the start of the month and admitted after the game that he still does not know the playbook.

On the first of Kiner’s right consecutive runs, the running back follows a lead block from Rouse on a power concept to pick up 12 yards. McDaniels went back to the same concept two plays later for five more yards, with Kiner breaking it back to run behind Pryor as he squared up five-time All-Pro DeMario Davis. And when Kiner cut one back two plays after that, Rouse provided one of the key blocks to create a lane.

No one would have predicted two months ago that this cast of characters would be on the field together to help finish out an AFC East victory for the Patriots. And yet, here they are, making plays when called upon and helping the team win.

Isn’t that a little bit romantic?

item.title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 7
item.description: The Giants are still in the top 20 — barely.
item.content:encoded:
No. 1 — San Francisco 49ers (6-0) | SAME

San Francisco remains the NFL’s hottest and most dangerous team. They play complementary football, and Brock Purdy is playing like one of the league’s best quarterbacks right now.

No. 2 —Buffalo Bills (5-1) | SAME

Buffalo traveled across the country and defeated a good Raiders team. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards with two touchdowns, including a crucial one to Keon Coleman. The 49ers and Bills remain the top two teams in the league.

No. 3 — Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) | SAME

Kansas City came out of the BYE week and beat up the lifeless Los Angeles Chargers, 22-6. The rushing attack continues to spearhead the Chiefs offense; Kenneth Walker III ran for 128 yards and scored two touchdowns to help secure the win.

No. 4 — Minnesota Vikings (5-0) | SAME

Minnesota had a BYE in Week 6.

No. 5 — Chicago Bears (4-2) | (10th) 📈 5 spots

Caleb Williams returned and was efficient, completing 30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown in Atlanta. The Falcons made it more interesting in the fourth quarter, but the Bears still escaped with a 31-23 victory.

No. 6 — New England Patriots (4-2) (9th) | 📈 3 spots

New England defeated the Jets, 26-19. The game was tight, but Drake Maye — who has played much better the last three weeks — found victory.

No. 7 — Denver Broncos (4-2) | (15th) 📈 8 spots

It doesn’t always look pretty — especially on offense — but a 17-14 victory against the Super Bowl champions is worth something. Sam Darnold threw two critical late interceptions that ended the Seahawks’ chances for a comeback, despite Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s 12 catches for 134 yards.

No. 8 —Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) | (7th) 📉 1 spot

Liam Coen’s offense dropped 31 points against the Texans in London. Cam Little kicked a go-ahead field goal with less than a minute in the game, but Texans’ kicker Ka’imi Fairbairn matched it to win the game for Houston, 34-31.

No. 9 — Seattle Seahawks (3-3) | (6th) 📉 3 spots

Seattle is still a top team in the NFL despite its .500 record. Sam Darnold has to take care of the football to allow their dominant defense to thrive.

No. 10 — Baltimore Ravens (4-2) | (8th) 📉 1 spot

The Ravens will get Lamar Jackson back soon, which will be a welcome change after a13-10 loss to Cleveland.

No. 11 — Green Bay Packers (4-2) | (17th) 📈 6 spots

Green Bay beat up the Cowboys, 23-13. Both Matthew Golden and Christian Watson were creating a bunch of separation, but their hands failed them multiple times; still, Golden went north of 100 yards on six catches, and Watson had 64 yards on three catches. The Packers’ defense stifled the Cowboys; Dak Prescott threw 54 passes in the game, and the end result was just 13 points.

No. 12— Carolina Panthers | (13th) 📈 1 spots

The Panthers went into Philadelphia and handled a very injured Eagles team, 25-14. Bryce Young threw for 281 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards with a score.

No. 13 — Detroit Lions (3-2) | (12th) 📉 1 spot

The Lions had their BYE in Week 6

No. 14 — Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) | SAME

The Pittsburgh Steelers escaped Tampa Bay with a 26-19 win, where the Buccaneers’ Jalon Daniels had a last-minute drive that Pittsburgh’s defense stopped. Aaron Rodgers threw for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception, as rookie receiver Germie Bernard caught 11 passes for 87 yards with a score.

No. 15 — Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) | (11th) 📉 4 spots

The Bengals were BYE in Week 6

No. 16 —Cleveland Browns (4-2) | (22nd) 📈 6 spots

The Browns won a classic, low-scoring 13-10 game over the Tyler Huntley-led Baltimore Ravens. Audric Esteme — who was signed earlier that week off the Vikings’ practice squad — ran in the go-ahead touchdown. Cleveland had two healthy backs and won with 164 passing yards; Jaleel McLaughlin led the rushing attack with just 41 yards.

No. 17 — Los Angeles Rams (2-4) | (5th) 📉 12 spots

The Rams were beaten by a six-field-goal effort off the foot of Chad Ryland. The Rams could not get much going against the Cardinals’ defense. The Rams totaled just 286 yards. A game to forget for a now sub-.500 Rams.

No. 18 — Houston Texans (2-4) | (21st) 📈 3 spots

The Texans defeated the Jaguars with a last-second field goal and are now on a two-game winning streak after starting 0-4. They host the Giants in Week 7.

No. 19 — Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) | (16th) 📉 4 spots

Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns, but also threw an interception. Tre Tucker had five catches for 97 yards with a pair of touchdowns. Michael Mayer led the tight ends with seven catches for 95 yards on nine targets. The Raiders have now lost three straight games — when will we see Francisco Mendoza?

No. 20 — New York Giants (3-2-1) | (18th) 📉 2 spots

The Giants are entertaining a QB question, but J.J. McCarthy sparked an impressive comeback effort that fell short. The Giants can’t run the football at all, and their ability to stop the run failed them against the Saints in the third quarter. However, their defense has a clear identity, and Malik Nabers/Isaiah Likely are playing out of their mind. They’re a resilient, competitive team, but they have serious question marks.

No. 21 — Atlanta Falcons (2-4)| (19th) 📉 2 spots

The Falcons mounted a comeback effort against the Bears with 16 points in the fourth quarter, but Chicago’s 27-7 lead was too much to overcome in the end. Still, the Falcons have two losses with Cooper Rush as their quarterback.

No. 22 — New Orleans Saints (2-4)| (27th) 📈 5 spots

I didn’t find the Saints all that impressive in their win against the Giants, but a road victory with more than 30 points is nothing to scoff at. The Saints need Tyler Shough to get healthy, and they would benefit from the return of Travis Etienne.

No. 23 — New York Jets (2-4) | (26) 📈 3 spot

The New York Jets lost in a competitive 26-19 game in Foxborough. Omar Cooper Jr. caught six passes for 103 yards with a long touchdown reception in his debut. Breece Hall should be returning from his quad injury soon.

No. 24 — Arizona Cardinals (2-4) | (29th) 📈 5 spots

The Arizona Cardinals shocked the NFL world by defeating the Rams on the road. Arizona’s defense stifled Matt Stafford and Sean McVay. Jeremiyah Love missed the game, but Bam Knight rushed for 80 yards, while Tyler Allgeier rushed for just 38 yards on 18 carries.

No. 25 — Dallas Cowboys (2-4) | (19th) 📉 6 spots

The Dallas Cowboys are broken on defense, and appear to be broken on offense. The Buccaneers stopped them for much of their Week 5 loss, and this Week 6 23-13 loss to Dallas was not much different. Dallas is struggling, as is the entire NFC East.

No. 26 — Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) (25th) 📉 3 spots

The Philadelphia Eagles are decimated by injuries, and Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood clots that will end his season. Tanner McKee is the quarterback, for now, and he threw for 215 yards with a touchdown. The offense could not do much in this 25-14 loss against Carolina. Philadelphia had just 222 yards on offense.

No. 27 — Washington Commanders (1-4-1) (25th) 📉 2 spots

Washington started to mount a comeback against the 49ers after sacking Brock Purdy to end the third quarter, which came after Stefon Diggs’ touchdown from Jayden Daniels. However, the 49ers — despite the injuries — held on and secured the win.

No. 28 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) | SAME

The Buccaneers made the game interesting against the Steelers, but they could not find a way to overcome their touchdown deficit, so the score ended 26-19. The Buccaneers turned the football over twice, and Jalon Daniels threw for 164 yards.

No. 29 —Indianapolis Colts (2-4) | (24th) 📉 5 spots

The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard after their second consecutive loss. Daniel Jones threw for 269 yards with a touchdown and a pair of interceptions. Jonathan Taylor did have 94 yards on 21 carries.

No. 30 — Tennessee Titans (1-5) | (32nd) 📈 2 spots

The Titans defeated the Colts — a Daboll vs. Daniel Jones matchup! Jones threw for 269 yards with a touchdown and a pair of interceptions. Jonathan Taylor did have 94 yards on 21 carries. Cam Ward, however, threw for just 102 yards and completed 11 passes; it was the Titans’ defense that forced three turnovers, and the Titans special teams that blocked a punt which helped Robert Saleh’s team secure their first win.

No. 31 — Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) | (30th) 📉 1 spots

The Chargers went down 19-3 and could not stop Kenneth Walker III on the ground. They remain the biggest disappointment in the NFL, as change might need ot happen soon.

No. 32 — Miami Dolphins (0-5) (31st) 📉 1 spot

The Titans won, and the Dolphins had their BYE in Week 6.
